teaser: Gameweek 9 throws up two 4/5 heavyweight clashes and leaves a handful of big names staring at **tough fixtures**. Knowing who to swerve matters as much as who to back this week.
fullWriteup:
The kind fixtures sit with **Aston Villa** (home to Fulham, 2/5), **Tottenham** (home to Palace, 2/5), Hull and Ipswich, and **Sunderland** away at Coventry. The pain is at the top: Liverpool vs Arsenal is 4/5 both ways, Chelsea vs Man United the same, and **Brighton** get the worst of the lot with a 5/5 trip to the Etihad. That's a problem if you own **De Cuyper** (42.5% owned) or Verbruggen, and it's a warning on Arsenal's defence — **Gabriel** and **Konsa** are both on form 9.0 but Anfield is no place for a clean sheet punt.

The players who combine form with a fixture worth having: **N.Jackson** (form 8.0, £6.8m) at home to Fulham on a 2/5 is the standout value pick, and **Evanilson** (form 8.3, 9.7% owned) hosts Leeds in a 3/5 that's far more inviting than anything the premium forwards get. **Haaland** is form 9.0 and 78.3% owned — Brighton at home on a 3/5 is comfortably the best fixture of any big hitter, so he keeps the armband.

For a differential, **McGinn** at £5.4m and just **3.2% owned** has form 5.7 and the same 2/5 home fixture as Jackson. Cheap way into the Villa game without paying up.
